items.title: AI May Be Making Publishing Easier, But It's Still Not Easy
items.excerpt: At the Media Transformation Summit cohosted by Publishing Signal, speakers agreed AI is accelerating production and lowering costs, but curation, audience-finding and judgement calls remain stubbornly human. One thread: AI systems favour content with explicit, machine-friendly structure, so publishers may have to rewrite how they present plot summaries, author bios and images online.

items.title: Applications Still Open for Korea's Asian Publishers Week 2026
items.excerpt: The Korea Publishers Society has extended its application deadline for Asian Publishers Week 2026 in Seoul, November 3-6, themed 'Publishing in the Era of AI: Between Crisis and Opportunity.' The programme frames AI as the organising question for Asian publishing rather than a side track.

items.title: 'Clarity of Thought and Responsibility': Can the Pope Move the Needle on AI Regulation?
items.excerpt: Publishing Perspectives reads Pope Leo XIV's May 29 encyclical as one of the most cogent arguments yet for an ethical framework around AI, and asks whether it can shift a regulatory debate that the book trade has been losing on copyright and creator consent.

items.title: European Union's AI Act requires transparency around specific types of AI-generated content
items.excerpt: The EU AI Act's transparency obligations cover AI-generated or AI-manipulated content that could be mistaken as real, pushing disclosure and labelling from a voluntary courtesy toward a compliance requirement for anyone publishing AI-assisted work into the EU.

items.title: Links of Interest: August 5, 2026
items.excerpt: Friedman's weekly round-up leads with poets discovering their copyrighted work inside Giggle Academy's learning materials, alongside publisher-side AI licensing moves. A snapshot of where authors are finding their text turning up without consent.

items.title: Indie Manga Publishers Join Forces, and Reading Gets Its Couch to 5K
items.excerpt: Five US indie manga publishers form the Indie Manga Alliance to pool resources against an industry squeezed by scale and machine translation, while Naomi Alderman launches an eight-week 'Couch to 5K' style programme to rebuild reading habits. The same round-up tracks the week's AI flashpoints in agenting and Amazon self-publishing.

items.title: These new features are coming to the iFlytek AINOTE 2
items.excerpt: iFlytek published a roadmap for its LLM-powered E Ink writing tablet, adding continuous pen-thickness control across notes, PDFs and e-books plus deeper automated note organisation and document processing. A look at what an AI-native reading-and-writing surface actually ships.

items.title: I Turned My Novel Into an AI Film, Here's How I Did It
items.excerpt: The Nerdy Novelist adapts one chapter of his sci-fi novel Jumpbox into an AI-generated film and breaks down the workflow that held up — and the shots that fell apart. A concrete look at novel-to-video AI pipelines from an author, not a studio.

items.title: 7 Mistakes That Scream "AI TEXT" (and How to Fix It)
items.excerpt: A craft-level breakdown of the seven tells that mark prose as machine-written, and line-edit fixes for each. Useful for the current wave of AI-detection disputes hitting authors and agents.

items.title: I Used AI to Write & Publish a Book in 30 Days (Here's What Happened...)
items.excerpt: Bestselling author Scott Allan walks through the exact framework used to write, edit and publish a complete nonfiction manuscript in 30 days with Claude, including where the human editing pass was non-negotiable.

items.title: How to Get Barnes & Noble to Host Your Book Signing | Self-Publishing News (August 6, 2026)
items.excerpt: This week's indie-author news covers ProWritingAid's new ProWritingMethod editing system plus platform updates from Apple Books, Lulu and Voices by INAudio, alongside Barnes & Noble tightening its local author-event rules.
